concepts.subject: Mathematics
concepts.name: Matrix multiplication and order
concepts.description: If A has order m × n and B has order n × p, the product AB is defined and has order m × p. Each entry is a row-by-column dot product. Matrix multiplication is generally not commutative: AB need not equal BA, and one product may be defined while the other is not.

concepts.subject: Mathematics
concepts.name: Increasing and decreasing functions
concepts.description: On an interval where a differentiable function has f'(x) > 0, it is increasing; where f'(x) < 0, it is decreasing. Critical points where f'(x) = 0 or is undefined divide the domain into intervals to test. A sign chart for the derivative supports the conclusion on each interval.

concepts.subject: Mathematics
concepts.name: Definite integrals and symmetry
concepts.description: A definite integral accumulates signed area over an interval and can be evaluated using an antiderivative: ∫_a^b f(x)dx = F(b) - F(a). Symmetry can simplify integrals: for an even function, ∫_-a^a f(x)dx = 2∫_0^a f(x)dx; for an odd function the integral over symmetric limits is zero. Check the function's parity before applying these properties.

concepts.subject: Mathematics
concepts.name: Continuity at a point
concepts.description: A function f is continuous at x = a when f(a) is defined, lim(x→a)f(x) exists, and that limit equals f(a). A graph may have a removable hole, jump, or unbounded behavior; each fails at least one part of the condition.

concepts.subject: Mathematics
concepts.name: Separation of variables
concepts.description: A differential equation is separable when it can be rearranged to place expressions involving y with dy and expressions involving x with dx. Integrate both sides and include a constant of integration. A solution may need to be checked against the original equation and any initial condition.

concepts.subject: Mathematics
concepts.name: Dot product and angle
concepts.description: For vectors a and b, a·b = |a||b|cosθ. In components, (a₁,a₂,a₃)·(b₁,b₂,b₃)=a₁b₁+a₂b₂+a₃b₃. A zero dot product indicates perpendicular nonzero vectors.

concepts.subject: Mathematics
concepts.name: Principal values of inverse sine
concepts.description: The inverse sine function returns a principal angle whose sine is the input. Its domain is [−1,1] and its principal-value range is [−π/2,π/2]. This restricted range makes arcsin a function even though sine itself is periodic and not one-to-one over all real numbers.

concepts.subject: Mathematics
concepts.name: Determinant and invertibility
concepts.description: A square matrix is invertible exactly when its determinant is nonzero. For a 2×2 matrix [[a,b],[c,d]], determinant is ad−bc. A zero determinant signals linearly dependent rows or columns and no inverse.

concepts.subject: Mathematics
concepts.name: Integration by substitution
concepts.description: Substitution simplifies an integral by setting u equal to an inner expression and replacing du consistently. It reverses the chain rule. For definite integrals, either change the limits to u-values or substitute back before applying the original limits.

concepts.subject: Mathematics
concepts.name: Order and degree
concepts.description: The order of a differential equation is the highest derivative present. The degree is the power of the highest-order derivative after the equation is expressed as a polynomial in derivatives, when that degree is defined. These are different classifications.

concepts.subject: Mathematics
concepts.name: Direction ratios and direction cosines
concepts.description: Direction ratios are any proportional triple describing a line’s direction. Direction cosines are cosines of the angles the direction makes with the coordinate axes and satisfy l²+m²+n²=1. Normalize direction ratios to obtain direction cosines.

concepts.subject: Mathematics
concepts.name: Area between curves
concepts.description: When two curves y=f(x) and y=g(x) bound a region from x=a to x=b and f is above g, its area is ∫_a^b [f(x)−g(x)]dx. If the curves cross, split the interval at intersections so the upper-minus-lower order is correct on each part.

concepts.subject: Mathematics
concepts.name: Feasible region and objective function
concepts.description: A linear programming problem optimizes a linear objective subject to linear constraints. The feasible region is the intersection of the constraint half-planes. For a bounded polygonal feasible region, an optimum occurs at a corner point; evaluate the objective at each feasible vertex.

concepts.subject: Mathematics
concepts.name: Conditional probability and independence
concepts.description: Conditional probability is P(A|B)=P(A∩B)/P(B) when P(B)>0. Events A and B are independent when learning that B occurred does not change the probability of A; equivalently P(A∩B)=P(A)P(B).
